title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Program Integrity Standard: Disregard Reduction on Weekly Payments after Misreported Earnings
content:
For a weekly payment on Unemployment Benefit Claims, the earnings disregard is reduced when the claimant's Benefit Overpayment Accounts include an overpayment caused by misreported earnings determined within the integrity window of 12 months before the handling date, read by determination date and balance due.

## Reduction

1. The disregard is reduced by 60.00 (the open integrity amount) when any such overpayment still carries a balance due above zero.
2. It is reduced by 40.00 (the repaid integrity amount) when such overpayments exist and every one of them carries no balance due.
3. No reduction applies when no overpayment caused by misreported earnings was determined within that window.

The integrity reduction is taken from the disregard first, counted earnings are measured against the reduced disregard, and the reduced disregard is never below zero.

## Hypothetical cases (disregard of 103.80 before reduction)

| Overpayments caused by misreported earnings | Disregard used |
|---|---|
| Determined 3 months ago, balance due 80.00 | 43.80 |
| Two determined within 12 months, both with no balance due | 63.80 |
| Determined 13 months ago, balance due 80.00 | 103.80 |
| None | 103.80 |

With counted earnings of 150.00, a disregard of 43.80 leaves 106.20 above it, against 46.20 with no reduction.
